Do you have to keep slamming your door to keep closed? - If your door won't stay closed or opens when your using your dryer, you need to replace the latches. It is very easy to do, unplug dryer first. You will need: straight slotted screw driver (regular type) and a pair of pliers. Lightweight Electric Stovetop - This is a fairly lightweight and portable electric cooking stove that plugs into any ordinary household outlet. It's lightweight construction has positives and negatives. It is light and easy to move around for when you aren't using it, but it also does not support very large pots/pans. So, if you think that you are going to be able to put a tea kettle on one burner and a full-sized skillet on the other burner you can forget about it. The heating elements are way too close together for large pots or pans, so you can only use one that is full-sized at a time.

The heating elements themselves are fairly small, so if you are trying to heat a large skillet it will only get to full temperature towards the center. For those of you who don't know the difference between a full-sized electric stove and one of these portable units you should keep in mind that most electric ovens with burners are directly connected to a dedicated 220V circuit, which gives them FAR more energy than a standard 110V power outlet. The result is that neither of the burners gets anywhere near as hot as the heating coils on an electric oven. Water takes longer to boil. Food takes longer to cook. So, be sure to allow for more cooking time than you normally would with an electric oven.

Despite its limitations, for its current price of around $23 this portable electric stove is a bargain. It's something that can easily be dragged into the back yard for BBQs or for plugging in anywhere outdoors. It is not perfect for every situation, but for some situations it works perfectly.

Go to that Tube channel and research and then buy every replaceable item while you got her open. - My 20 year old dryer decided that it was going to heat at it's hottest setting to the point of scalding my hands when removing the clothes from the dryer and causing a major case of wrinkles in my work Polo's. After going to YouTube to find out how to diagnose the issue, I found that there are a few things to check. First thing you will need to do is open the back of the dryer, with it unplugged, and check the Thermal Fuse. This can be done with a multi-meter or temporarily jump the two connectors/blade terminals and check if the Dryer runs at the correct temp for all cycles. Since I had the dryer taken apart I figured I would clean out the blower fan area and the fan ducting as well as the entire "innards" of the dryer. After temporarily jumping the thermal fuse I found that it had kicked the bucket as the dryer started to work again due to jumping out the fuse. Did I say that this dryer is 20 years old and the original fuse lasted that long? So I decided that since I have the thing open I might as well replace the other 20 Year old electrical components that were back there. These Items included: the Thermal Fuse, Cycling Thermostat, High Limit Dryer Thermostat and Dryer Thermal cut off. Each have their own job and purpose, so don't skimp out and think you can get away with changing the item that has failed, because if that item failed the others will follow. Did I mention my Dryer is 20 years old? As A side note; I also checked the Heating Element and found that one of the coils had warped and contacted/welded itself the the element body, this is what took out the fuse. A pair of needle nose pliers and a steady hand detached the coil and re-positioned the coil in its original shape and placement. My 20 year old dryer, that was a wedding gift to my wife when she married her fist husband now works like a champ!

I just did a few loads with the Wonderwash and am satisfied with it - I am a student who lives in an apartment without washer/dryer and don't have a car to go to the laundromat. I just did a few loads with the Wonderwash and am satisfied with it. The assembly is easy, the size of the item is both sufficiently small to be used on a kitchen top yet big enough to wash a few days worth of laundry.

Make sure you put the Wonderwash on a wet surface so that the suction pad can maintain the item while spinning. Also, do not start cracking it too fast too soon, build up the speed gradually.

Personally, I put the detergent first, then fill the Wonderwash half with hot water, add the clothes and give a few spins to pre treat. After 5-10 mins, I start spinning continually for 10 mins. It is not hard to do, when the movement is started you barely feel the weight. Once again, make sure your suction pads will hold it in place. The cap does not leak and the tube provided to drain the water is very efficient.

So far, the only real con is that when you are done, the clothes are so wet, you have to hang them above a tub for a few hours before they are fully drained.

I'll keep this review updated.
